summary: In Arizona, Medicaid (AHCCCS) covers doula care with no visit limit: $16.28 per 15 minutes for prenatal and postpartum visits and $781.32 for labor and delivery, with a provider referral.
payment_notes: $16.28 per 15 minutes for prenatal and postpartum visits (T1032, up to 2 hours / 8 units per day without prior authorization) and a flat $781.32 for labor and delivery (T1033, once per 9 months). Rates unchanged for FFY25, FFY26 and FFY27 (effective 10/1/2026). There is no cap on the number of visits, so there is no fixed per-pregnancy maximum.
certification_required: Arizona Dept. of Health Services (ADHS) state doula certification (national/other certifications alone do not qualify), then registration as an AHCCCS provider

summary: In Arkansas, Medicaid covers doula care: up to $933.20 per pregnancy for 6 prenatal and postpartum visits, plus support during labor and delivery.
payment_notes: $64.45 per prenatal/postpartum visit (minimum 60 minutes; up to 6 combined) plus one flat labor and delivery payment that depends on the type of birth: $468.55 vaginal, $325.45 cesarean, $527.78 vaginal birth after a prior cesarean (VBAC), $546.50 cesarean after an attempted VBAC. Standard-package totals: $855.25 (vaginal), $712.15 (cesarean), $914.48 (VBAC), $933.20 (cesarean after attempted VBAC, the highest). Rates are from the DHS Supportive Maternal Care fee schedule (run 08/27/26). More than 6 visits only through a DHS extension of benefits.
certification_required: Arkansas Dept. of Health Certified Community-Based Doula certification (through the Doula Alliance of Arkansas or another ADH-designated certifying organization; $50 fee), age 18+, NPI

summary: In California, Medicaid covers doula care: up to $3,263.31 per pregnancy under the standard recommendation, for an initial visit, 8 prenatal or postpartum visits and 2 extended postpartum visits, plus support during labor and delivery.
payment_notes: Medi-Cal fee-for-service rates since the 1/1/2024 Targeted Rate Increase (unchanged in the October 2026 fee schedule): initial visit $197.98; each prenatal/postpartum visit $162.11 (up to 8, any mix); extended 3-hour postpartum visit $486.36 (up to 2); labor and delivery support $685.07 (vaginal) or $795.73 (cesarean); miscarriage or abortion support $250.85. Standing-recommendation package total: $3,152.65 with a vaginal birth, $3,263.31 with a cesarean. Up to 9 more postpartum visits (about $1,458.99 more) need a second recommendation.
certification_required: Training pathway (16+ hours of core training plus support at 3+ births) or experience pathway (5 years of doula work in the past 7 plus 3 letters); adult/infant CPR; basic HIPAA training; age 18+; 3 hours of continuing education every 3 years

summary: In Colorado, Medicaid covers doula care: up to $1,470 per pregnancy for up to 3 hours of prenatal and 3 hours of postpartum visits, plus support during labor and delivery.
payment_notes: Since 7/1/2026: $24.50 per 15 minutes (T1032) for up to 180 minutes of prenatal care and up to 180 minutes of postpartum care (12 units each; $294 each), plus a flat $882 for labor and delivery (T1033), for $1,470 total. Earlier rates: $25.00 and $900 ($1,500 total) at launch and again from 10/1/2025; briefly $25.40 and $914.40 for 7/1/2025 to 9/30/2025.
certification_required: Health First Colorado doula enrollment through a certification pathway (training from an HCPF-approved organization, e.g. DONA or CAPPA) or an experience pathway; Doula Code of Conduct; fingerprint background check; Type 1 NPI

summary: In Connecticut, Medicaid covers doula care: up to $1,200 per pregnancy for 4 prenatal or postpartum visits, plus support during labor and delivery.
payment_notes: $100 per perinatal (prenatal or postpartum) visit, up to 4 combined (T1033), plus a flat $800 for in-person attendance at labor and delivery (T1033-HD): up to $1,200 total. Up to 4 more perinatal visits ($400) are possible with prior authorization.
certification_required: Connecticut Dept. of Public Health doula certification (approved training program plus 2 reference letters, or notarized attestation of serving 3+ families and training in 4+ core competencies); $100 DPH application fee; NPI

summary: In Delaware, Medicaid covers doula care: up to $1,046.88 per pregnancy for 3 prenatal and 3 postpartum visits, plus support during labor and delivery.
payment_notes: $15.83 per 15 minutes for up to 3 prenatal and 3 postpartum visits of up to 90 minutes each ($94.98 per visit), plus a flat $477 for labor and birth: $1,046.88 for the standard package. Extras not counted: a $100 incentive when the same doula does all 6 visits plus the birth, and up to 5 more postpartum visits ($474.90) with a practitioner's recommendation (since 4/2/2025). Rates are from Delaware First Health's provider page.
certification_required: Delaware Certification Board 'Certified Doula for Medicaid Reimbursement' (regular pathway: 16 hours of training + 3 births; or legacy pathway: 15 clients + 9 births in 3 years); adult/infant CPR; 1-hour HIPAA training; liability insurance ($1M/$3M); fingerprint background check; NPI

summary: In the District of Columbia, Medicaid covers up to 12 doula visits including the birth, paying $107.89 per visit during pregnancy or the first 6 weeks after birth, $762.98 for labor and delivery, and $13.48 per 15 minutes for later postpartum visits.
payment_notes: CY2026 rates (effective 1/1/2026, +2.7%): $107.89 per perinatal visit; $762.98 flat for labor and delivery (vaginal, cesarean or VBAC); postpartum visits $13.48 per 15 minutes, up to 24 units (6 hours, $323.52) per visit. Up to 12 visits total, including the birth. Theoretical maximum with labor support: $762.98 + 11 six-hour postpartum visits = $4,321.70. A $100 incentive is paid on top if the mom also attends an OB postpartum visit 7 to 84 days after delivery.
certification_required: Current certification from a DHCF-approved doula certifying organization; age 18+; high school diploma or equivalent; liability insurance ($1M per occurrence / $3M aggregate); NPI

summary: In Florida, every Medicaid health plan offers doula services as an extra benefit, with visits and pay set by each plan; moms in fee-for-service Medicaid aren't covered.
payment_notes: No state fee schedule. Doula services are an optional 'expanded benefit' that each Medicaid managed care (SMMC) health plan offers and pays for under rates it negotiates with doulas. All 8 SMMC health plans list doula services on AHCA's grid effective 2/1/2025.
certification_required: Set by each Medicaid health plan (no state doula certification or Medicaid doula credential)

summary: In Illinois, Medicaid covers doula care with no visit limit: $15 per 15 minutes for prenatal and postpartum visits and $720 for labor and delivery, under a statewide standing recommendation.
payment_notes: $15 per 15 minutes for prenatal education (S9445, up to 2 hours per day), postpartum support (S9444, up to 4 hours per day) and miscarriage/abortion support (T1032, up to 2 hours per day); group sessions $5 per 15 minutes. Flat $720 for labor and delivery support (once per pregnancy). $50 each for going with the mom to up to 2 postpartum OB visits and $50 for the baby's first newborn visit. Daily caps took effect 5/1/2026; rates unchanged since 2/1/2024. There is no limit on the number of visits, so there is no per-pregnancy maximum.
certification_required: Illinois Medicaid-Certified Doula certificate from the SIU School of Medicine program (training pathway: approved training + 3 doula experiences in the past 12 months; or legacy pathway: 5 experiences in 3 years); CPR/BLS, HIPAA, cultural competency/implicit bias and trauma-informed care training; age 18+; no fee; renew every 3 years; NPI

summary: In Kansas, Medicaid covers doula care: up to $1,295 per pregnancy for about 7 hours of prenatal and 6 hours of postpartum visits, plus support during labor and delivery.
payment_notes: $15 per 15 minutes (T1032) for up to 28 units (7 hours) of prenatal visits and up to 25 units (6.25 hours) of postpartum visits per pregnancy, plus a flat $500 for labor and delivery (T1033): up to $1,295 total. Rates are from KMAP Bulletin 24099 (May 2024); a Nov 2025 bulletin (25256) says billing guidelines are unchanged.
certification_required: Certification from a doula training organization (pathway 1) or at least 30 hours of training (pathway 2), plus a signed attestation of supporting at least 3 births; Type 1 NPI (taxonomy 374J00000X)

summary: Kentucky Medicaid doesn't cover doula care.
payment_notes: No Medicaid doula benefit. Moms on Medicaid pay a doula out of pocket or use a free or sliding-scale community program.

summary: In Louisiana, Medicaid covers doula care: up to $1,016.52 per pregnancy for 5 prenatal and 3 postpartum visits, plus support during labor and delivery.
payment_notes: $69.69 per prenatal or postpartum visit (S9445; up to 5 prenatal + 3 postpartum, each up to 90 minutes) and $459 flat for attending labor and delivery (99199, vaginal or cesarean); up to $1,016.52 total. Doulas can also bill up to 3 birthing, 3 lactation and 3 parenting classes at $40.80 each (S9442/S9443/S9444), which would add $367.20 (max $1,383.72 with classes). Rates effective 1/1/2026 on the Louisiana Medicaid professional services fee schedule (current edition effective 7/1/2026).
certification_required: Approved registration with the Louisiana Doula Registry Board, plus enrollment as a Louisiana Medicaid provider (individual or doula group)

summary: Maine Medicaid doesn't cover doulas yet; the state started setting rates in December 2025 and plans to start paying in 2028 if funded.
payment_notes: No rates yet. MaineCare started a rate determination for doula services on 12/30/2025, and the effective date is listed as TBD.

summary: In Maryland, Medicaid covers doula care: up to $1,427.84 per pregnancy for 8 prenatal or postpartum visits, plus support during labor and delivery.
payment_notes: Prenatal visits $16.62 per 15-minute unit (T1032) and postpartum visits $19.62 per unit (T1032 U9), up to 4 units (1 hour) per visit; up to 8 prenatal and postpartum visits in any combination; $800 flat for attending labor and delivery (T1033, raised from $350 on 7/1/2023). Total ranges from $1,331.84 (all prenatal) to $1,427.84 (all postpartum).
certification_required: Current certification from a Maryland Medicaid-approved doula certification organization, age 18+, background check, liability insurance, NPI, and enrollment through ePREP

summary: In Massachusetts, Medicaid covers doula care: up to $1,700 per pregnancy for up to 8 hours of prenatal and postpartum visits, plus support during labor and delivery.
payment_notes: $100 per perinatal visit up to 60 minutes, or $150 per visit of 61 to 90 minutes, with perinatal visit payments capped at $800 per pregnancy (8 hours of visits without prior authorization); $900 for labor and delivery support. Up to $1,700 total. More visits are possible with prior authorization. Rates set by 101 CMR 319.00, effective 12/8/2023.
certification_required: Age 18+, NPI, the free online MassHealth Doula Provider Training, and required competencies shown through the Formal Training Pathway (training certificate or doula certification) or the Experience Pathway (3 client + 2 licensed-provider recommendations from the past 5 years)

summary: In Michigan, Medicaid covers doula care: up to $2,700 per pregnancy for 12 prenatal or postpartum visits, plus support during labor and delivery.
payment_notes: $100 per prenatal or postpartum visit (S9445 HD, up to 12 combined) and $1,500 for labor and delivery support (T1033 HD); up to $2,700 total. Up to 6 more visits with prior authorization. Rates effective 10/1/2024 (MMP 24-40); before that, $75 per visit for up to 6 visits and $700 for labor ($1,150 total). Confirmed on the January 2026 doula fee schedule.
certification_required: Listed on the MDHHS Doula Registry (age 18+, high school diploma or equivalent, certificate from an MDHHS-approved doula training program), then NPI, SIGMA and CHAMPS enrollment; must contract with each Medicaid Health Plan to serve its members

summary: In Minnesota, Medicaid has covered doula care since 2014, paying $100 per prenatal or postpartum visit and $1,400 for support at the birth.
payment_notes: $100 per prenatal or postpartum visit and $1,400 for attending the birth, effective 1/1/2024 (Minn. Stat. 256B.758(b); SPA MN-23-0018). Before that, $47 per visit and $488 for the birth. We couldn't confirm the per-pregnancy visit limit from a state source, so no total is given. The National Health Law Program reports up to 18 prenatal and postpartum visits since May 2024, which would mean up to $3,200.
certification_required: Certification from a doula certification organization designated by the Minnesota Dept. of Health, plus listing on the MDH Doula Registry (criminal background check, $200 fee, renew every 3 years); enroll as an MHCP provider

summary: Mississippi Medicaid doesn't cover doula care.
payment_notes: No Medicaid doula benefit. Moms on Medicaid pay a doula out of pocket or use a free or sliding-scale community program.

summary: In Missouri, Medicaid covers doula care: up to $1,250 per pregnancy for 6 prenatal or postpartum visits, plus support during labor and delivery.
payment_notes: $75 per prenatal or postpartum support session (S9445 TH/TS, 60+ minutes; 6 combined) and $800 for attending the birth (T1033, up to 24 hours; planned or unplanned C-sections paid the same since 12/15/2025) = $1,250. Also billable: up to 2 lactation visits at $50 (S9443) and up to 10 community-navigation units at $25 (S9482), for a $1,600 maximum. Births longer than 24 hours can add $5 per 15 minutes (T1032, up to 95 units).
certification_required: Age 18+, current certificate from a recognized national or Missouri-based doula training organization that meets MO HealthNet curriculum standards (or listing on the Missouri Community Doula Council roster), 6 CE hours per year, liability insurance; enroll as a MO HealthNet provider

summary: Montana Medicaid doesn't cover doulas yet; a 2025 law allows coverage and doula licensing starts January 1, 2027.
payment_notes: No Medicaid doula rates published.
certification_required: Montana doula license from the Dept. of Labor & Industry (required to practice as a doula starting 1/1/2027)

summary: Nebraska passed a 2026 law requiring Medicaid to pay for doula services by January 1, 2029; rates and rules aren't set yet.
payment_notes: No rates yet. The law says DHHS will set rates and pay them with state funds; a work group's implementation plan, due 1/1/2027, will recommend rates.

summary: In Nevada, Medicaid covers doula care: up to $1,430 per pregnancy for 4 prenatal or postpartum visits, plus support during labor and delivery.
payment_notes: $100 per prenatal or postpartum visit (S9445; up to 4 combined, postpartum visits up to 90 days after birth) and $900 for labor and delivery = $1,300 for members in urban Washoe and Clark counties. Members living elsewhere get 10% more ($110 per visit, $990 labor) = $1,430. Rates effective 10/1/2023 (SPA NV-23-0016); before that, $350 total. Still current on the July 2026 PT 90 fee schedule.
certification_required: Doula certification from the Nevada Certification Board or another state-approved training program (changed 5/27/2026); enroll as Nevada Medicaid provider type 90

summary: New Hampshire has federal approval to cover doula care in Medicaid (up to 8 visits plus the birth), but no sign yet that it's paying doulas.
payment_notes: SPA public notice fee schedule: $12.50 per 15 minutes for visits (T1032) and $500 per diem for birth support (T1033). Up to 8 prenatal/postpartum visits per pregnancy, with more allowed by prior authorization. The state sets no per-pregnancy dollar cap.
certification_required: Voluntary NH state doula certification from the Office of Professional Licensure and Certification (OPLC), required for Medicaid billing

summary: In New Jersey, Medicaid covers doula care: up to $1,065 per pregnancy for 8 prenatal or postpartum visits, plus support during labor and delivery.
payment_notes: $16.62 per 15-minute unit: initial prenatal visit up to 6 units ($99.72), other visits up to 4 units ($66.48); $500 flat for attending the delivery. Standard care: up to 8 visits + delivery = up to $1,065. Enhanced care for members 19 or younger: up to 12 visits + delivery = up to $1,331. A separate $100 incentive is paid if the doula makes a postpartum visit and the member sees an OB clinician postpartum. Rates effective 7/1/2022 (SPA NJ-22-0020).
certification_required: Completion of an NJ FamilyCare-approved community doula training (including HIPAA and adult/infant CPR), age 18+, fingerprint-based background check, liability insurance ($1M/$3M); enroll as an NJ FamilyCare fee-for-service provider

summary: In New Mexico, Medicaid covers doula care: up to $3,300 per pregnancy for nine 2-hour prenatal or postpartum visits a year, plus support during labor and delivery.
payment_notes: $25 per 15 minutes ($100/hour) for prenatal and postpartum visits (T1032 U1), up to 2 hours per day and nine 2-hour visits per calendar year (up to $1,800); $1,500 flat for labor and delivery support (T1033 U3). Up to $3,300. Counseling for pre-conception, pregnancy loss, infant loss or termination is billed separately (T1032 U2). Extra visits need documented medical necessity.
certification_required: NM Department of Health Certified Doula (one of 3 pathways: certified training, core-competency training + 3 clients, or experience with 3 recommendations + 3 clients), age 18+, adult/infant CPR, HIPAA training, local business license and FEIN; 24 CE hours every 2 years; then enroll with NM Medicaid and credential with each MCO

summary: In New York, Medicaid covers doula care: up to $1,500 per pregnancy for 8 prenatal or postpartum visits, plus support during labor and delivery.
payment_notes: New York City: $93.75 per perinatal visit (T1032, at least 30 minutes; up to 8 prenatal and postpartum visits combined) + $750 for in-person labor and delivery support (T1033) = $1,500. Rest of state: $84.37 per visit + $675 = $1,349.96. Fee schedule effective 3/1/2024.
certification_required: Age 18+, NPI, adult/infant CPR, doula liability insurance, HIPAA familiarity; Training Pathway (24 hours of competency training + support at 3 births) or Work Experience Pathway (30 births or 1,000 hours in the last 10 years + 3 recommendations)

summary: In Ohio, Medicaid covers doula care: up to $1,200 per pregnancy for up to 12 hours of prenatal and postpartum visits, plus support during labor and delivery.
payment_notes: $12.50 per 15-minute unit for prenatal and postpartum support (HCPCS T1032), up to 48 units (12 hours, $600) without prior authorization, plus a $600 flat per-birth payment for labor and delivery (T1033) regardless of how long labor lasts. Up to $1,200 per pregnancy and postpartum period. More units can be approved through prior authorization. Rates unchanged since 10/3/2024.
certification_required: Ohio Board of Nursing doula certificate (age 18+, $35 fee): current certification from a recognized doula organization plus 4 hours of racial bias/health disparities/cultural competency training, or 3 years of practice plus 10 hours of education

summary: In Oklahoma, SoonerCare covers 8 prenatal or postpartum doula visits plus labor and delivery support with a referral form; the state doesn't publish doula dollar rates.
payment_notes: Paid as a percentage of the SoonerCare physician fee schedule: 40% for prenatal/postpartum visits (59899-HD), 65% for vaginal delivery support (59409/59612/59620-HD) and 40% for cesarean-only support (59514-HD). OHCA does not publish the doula (HD-modifier) dollar amounts. The National Health Law Program lists $64.45 per visit and $528.85 for a vaginal delivery ($1,044.45 total), but OHCA's documents don't show those amounts.
certification_required: Age 18+, NPI, and a birth, postpartum, full-spectrum or community-based doula certification from an OHCA-recognized organization (list on OHCA doula page)

summary: In Oregon, Medicaid covers doula care: up to $2,365 per pregnancy for 2 prenatal visits, 2 postpartum visits and 4 more in any mix, plus support during labor and delivery.
payment_notes: $1,505 global package covering 2 prenatal visits, support on the day of delivery and 2 postpartum visits, plus up to 4 more visits in any prenatal/postpartum mix at $215 each. Up to $2,365 total. If the full package isn't delivered, billing is itemized at $645 for delivery-day support and $215 per visit. Fee-for-service (open card) rates effective 1/1/2025. Billed once per pregnancy, with no extra pay for multiples.
certification_required: Oregon Traditional Health Worker certified birth doula (OHA): 28-hour approved training plus cultural responsiveness, HIPAA, trauma-informed care and oral health training, 3 births and 3 postpartum visits, CPR; legacy (experience) and reciprocity pathways

summary: In Pennsylvania, Medicaid covers doula care: up to $2,200 per pregnancy for 12 prenatal or postpartum visits a year, plus support during labor and delivery.
payment_notes: $100 per prenatal or postpartum visit (T1032-U7/U8), with a combined limit of 12 visits per calendar year, plus a $1,000 flat rate for labor and delivery (T1033), one per pregnancy. Up to $2,200 for the standard package. Separately, up to 2 'other services' visits per year at $175 each cover fertility/pre-conception counseling, pregnancy loss, infant loss or termination. These are fee-for-service rates effective 1/1/2025.
certification_required: Certified Perinatal Doula credential from the Pennsylvania Certification Board (24 hours of training or experience pathway, CPR, 3 client evaluations)

summary: In Rhode Island, Medicaid covers doula care: up to $1,500 per pregnancy for 3 prenatal and 3 postpartum visits, plus support during labor and delivery.
payment_notes: Capped at $1,500 per pregnancy for 3 prenatal visits, 1 labor and delivery visit and 3 postpartum visits, with no prior authorization. Visits must be at least 60 minutes. The National Health Law Program gives the split as $100 per prenatal/postpartum visit and $900 for labor and delivery.
certification_required: Certified Perinatal Doula (CPD) credential from the Rhode Island Certification Board (20 hours of training, CPR, ServSafe food handling)

summary: South Carolina Medicaid doesn't cover doula care.
payment_notes: No Medicaid doula benefit. Moms on Medicaid pay a doula out of pocket or use a free or sliding-scale community program.

summary: In South Dakota, Medicaid covers doula care: up to $1,800 per pregnancy for prenatal and postpartum visits billed by the quarter hour, plus support during labor and delivery.
payment_notes: $17.32 per 15 minutes for prenatal, postpartum or care-coordination support (T1032) and $616.01 flat for labor and delivery (T1033), both effective 7/1/2026; earlier rates were $16.87 and $600. Capped at $1,800 per pregnancy, which can be exceeded only with prior authorization.
certification_required: Age 18+ and current certification from an SD Medicaid-recognized organization (e.g. DONA, CAPPA, BirthWorks, ICEA dual, MaternityWise, DTI, Childbirth Professionals International, Birthing Advocacy Doula Training) while a state oversight body is set up

summary: Tennessee Medicaid doesn't cover doula care.
payment_notes: No Medicaid doula benefit. Moms on Medicaid pay a doula out of pocket or use a free or sliding-scale community program.

summary: Texas Medicaid doesn't pay for doula support during labor and birth. Since December 1, 2024, certified doulas can enroll in Texas Medicaid as case managers (Case Management for Children and Pregnant Women) to help higher-risk pregnant members get medical and social services.
payment_notes: No Medicaid doula benefit for labor and birth support. Since December 1, 2024, a certified doula can enroll as a Case Management for Children and Pregnant Women (CPW) provider and bill case-management visits; that pays for case management, not birth support. Moms on Medicaid pay a doula out of pocket or use a free or sliding-scale community program.

summary: In Utah, Medicaid has covered doula care since April 1, 2026, including up to 8 hours of prenatal and postpartum visits and labor support; rates are listed only in the state's lookup tool.
payment_notes: Prenatal and postpartum support is billed in 15-minute units (T1032), limited to 32 units (8 hours) per rolling year. Labor support is one per-diem payment per pregnancy (T1033). Dollar rates are published only in Utah's online coverage and reimbursement lookup tool.
certification_required: Enroll with Utah Medicaid via the Doula Provider Attestation: approved doula training plus 3 births in 5 years and CPR (certification pathway), or 10 births (5 in the last 2 years) plus 4 recommendation letters and CPR (experience pathway)

summary: Vermont passed a 2025 law requiring Medicaid to cover certified doulas once federal approval comes through; it isn't paying yet.
payment_notes: No rates yet. Act 50 says it is the legislature's intent that DVHA pay 'reasonable and adequate' rates consistent with other states' Medicaid doula rates. Travel time and mileage are not reimbursable.
certification_required: State certification as a community-based perinatal doula (Office of Professional Regulation, 26 V.S.A. ch. 84)

summary: In Virginia, Medicaid covers up to 8 prenatal or postpartum doula visits plus attendance at the birth, through 6 months after delivery; current dollar rates aren't published.
payment_notes: Visits are billed in 15-minute units: up to 6 units for the first prenatal visit and 4 units for each other visit, plus attendance at birth, and up to two value-based incentive payments (linkage to the mom's postpartum visit and the baby's pediatric visit). DMAS's 2022 doula flyer says Medicaid reimbursed $859 for 8 prenatal/postpartum visits and delivery, plus up to $100 in incentives. DMAS doesn't publish current doula rates; its fee files list the codes as individually priced.
certification_required: Virginia state-certified community doula (Virginia Certification Board; 60 hours of VDH-approved training; $100 fee) plus $1M/$3M liability insurance to enroll

summary: In Washington, Medicaid covers doula care: up to $3,500 per pregnancy for an intake visit and up to 20 hours of prenatal and postpartum visits, plus support during labor and delivery.
payment_notes: $750 for one in-person prenatal intake visit of at least 2 hours (59899-U1), $750 flat for continuous in-person labor and delivery support (T1033), and $25 per 15 minutes (T1032) for up to 20 hours (80 units) of other prenatal and postpartum visits, of which 6 units are set aside for a comprehensive postpartum visit. Up to $3,500 per pregnancy. Fee schedule effective 1/1/2025.
certification_required: Washington state-certified birth doula (Dept. of Health), NPI, and ProviderOne enrollment

payment_notes: No Medicaid doula benefit. Moms on Medicaid pay a doula out of pocket or use a free or sliding-scale community program.
